## Verified and completed — browser content transition batch

Immutable [41246979957](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/actions/runs/41246979957), attempt 1 at `6eaac5e01e5631d567e571c32d6523d663a8a184`, **passed**: JS 2/2 and Wasm 2/2, two original XML reports, zero failures/errors/skips. These are **two distinct methods / four actual target executions**, not four new methods. Gradle exits 0 in 263.07s and 270.07s respectively. Both actual hosts report Chrome156.0.8078.47 and JDK17.0.21.

All three original acceptance criteria were independently reviewed against source and original results:
- Direct and remembered Data→Url→Data transitions execute through the public library and actual connected native documents.
- Navigator and state paths produce matching iframe attributes and page content; inline HTML cannot override a subsequent URL.
- Genuine cross-origin CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'` and X-Frame-Options `DENY` responses cannot retain or misreport old documents/metadata. Trusted positive messaging, actual HTTP request/header receipts, newer native loads, denied-message absence through a later receipt barrier and inline recovery are checked; cross-origin unreadability alone is not treated as proof.

Complete native methods include viewport disposal, load/message listener removal and bounded HTTP fixture-session cleanup under NonCancellable. Exact1012 library/1089 combined inputs match immutable Git; original ZIP/XML identities, task freshness and runtime/daemon agreement were verified. Public APIs/signatures remain compatible.

**Closed immediately after verification/readback, before follow-up documentation.** Original issue body, title, labels, attribution and upstream references are unchanged. Prior 41245182190 startup failures remain failed; the owning empty DI metadata repair and reviewer-only Chrome-label refusal remain preserved. No accepted unrelated suites were replayed.

Scope: Chromium JS/Wasm content contracts only, not other engines or adjacent #64/#65/#40, memory/ABI/packaged-consumer/dependency/legal/security/release readiness. No packages, deployment, Pages or releases were published.
